findings.reason: a node implementing to the Why's 92% figure either reddens its own first case against a 20-point reserve it was never told about, or concludes the zeroing belongs at the refusal site in `dispatch_admission.py`/`budget_group.py`, outside its declared fence; naming the third reserve (or stating that the case's group is all-review-member review-excluded, so its bookend reserve is already zero) is what removes that fork.
findings.text: §48's Why sizes the ceiling as "100% less the 5% resume and 3% coordinator reserves" and names only those two, but `reckon/crew/reserve.py` applies a third reserve, `bookend_reserve_pct` (default 20.0 points), and `_refuse_against_the_bookend_reserve` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:293`) holds a fresh implement dispatch that far below the ceiling at every utilisation; so an advisory group that is not all-review-excluded is still held at 96%, the section's own first case ("An advisory group at 96% with a burn multiple of 19 is not held for an implement dispatch", plan.html:632) fails unless the third reserve is also zeroed, and the write-paths sentence (plan.html:627) names `reckon/crew/budget_lift.py` as "where the group's effective block is resolved" while the resolution dispatch actually takes composes the bookend rule in `reckon/crew/budget_group.py`'s `effective_block` (reckon/crew/budget_group.py:186), a module the section does not declare

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/pace_report.py` exists with `pace_hold` at :1252, `_hold_marker` resolves in `reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:928` and `effective_budget` at :553, `budget-fits-a-worker-window` §2 exists and is declared done, and the new test file is the node's own deliverable, correctly absent.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the node declares a negative control ("Apply the pace hold to an advisory group, and the first case must fail. Separately, keep the reserves for an advisory group, and the second case must fail", plan.html:642), so its gate can show each guard fires, and the five cases are measurable assertions.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate logs ("Both arms' logs go in the run directory", plan.html:639) and the evidence fragment are durable run-directory paths, not a node-local or session-scratch path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section's new symbols and keys (`pace: advisory`, `test_a_metered_lanes_pace_can_be_advice.py`) are mechanism names carrying no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the Why enumerates two reserves ("the 5% resume and 3% coordinator reserves", plan.html:619) but a third reserve is applied to a non-bookend dispatch, so the deliverable's "carries no reserves" (plan.html:622) is not produced by the mechanism the section names.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the node carries one deliverable, "A budget group can declare its pace advisory" (plan.html:620); the host-flight declaration is named as the coordinator's step, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s48's `plan-section-depends-on` entry `["lane-and-model-routing#s46", "budget-fits-a-worker-window#s2"]` (plan.html:22) records both edges the section's new write-paths sentence relies on, and both targets exist and are declared done.
